(Ṭhāṇa 989) In the continent of Jambudvīpa, in the region of Bhārata, ten Kulakaras will appear in the future Utsarpiṇī; namely: Sīmaṅkara, Sīmandhara, Khemaṅkara, Khemandhara, Vimalavāhana, Saṃmuti, Paḍisuta, Daḍhadhanu, Dasadhanu, and Satadhanu.

On the island of Jambudvīpa, to the east of Mount Mandara, on both banks of the great river Sītā, ten mountain ranges (Vakṣāraparvatas) are described, namely: Mālyavanta, Cittakūṭa, Pamhakūṭa, Nalinakūṭa, Ekaśaila, Trikūṭa, Vaiśramaṇakūṭa, Añjana, Māyāñjana, and Saumanasa.

On the island of Jambudvīpa, to the west of Mount Mandara, on both banks of the great river Sītodā, ten range-mountains (vakkhārapavvata) are described, namely: Vijjuppabha, Akāvatī, Pamhāvatī, Āsīvisa, Suhāvahe, Candapavvata, Sūrapavvata, Nāgapavvata, Dēvapavvata, and Gandhamādana. In the same manner, the range-mountains are to be mentioned for the eastern half of Ghāyaisaṇḍa, up to the western half of Pukkhavaradvīvaḍḍha.
Ten kalpas presided over by Indras are taught, namely: Sōhamma up to Sahassāra, Pāṇata, and Accuta. In these ten kalpas, ten Indras are taught, namely: Sakka, Īsāṇa, up to Accuta.
For these ten Indras, ten *parijāniya* celestial palaces are taught, namely: Pālaē, Pupphaē, up to Vimalavara and Savvatōbhadda.
The tenth-daśamika (*dasadasamiyā*) monk’s vow (*bhikkhupaḍimā*) is accomplished according to the scripture, up to being fully mastered, in one hundred and fifty nights and five hundred alms-rounds.

Ten types of living beings involved in the cycle of existence are taught, namely: first-moment one-sensed beings, non-first-moment one-sensed beings, and so on, up to non-first-moment five-sensed beings.

Ten types of all living beings are taught, namely: earth-bodied beings up to plant-bodied beings, two-sensed beings up to five-sensed beings, and those without senses (non-sensed beings). Alternatively, ten types of all living beings are taught, namely: first-moment hell-beings, non-first-moment hell-beings, and so on, up to non-first-moment gods, first-moment perfected beings, and non-first-moment perfected beings.
For a human being with a lifespan of one hundred years, ten stages are taught (as follows):
childhood, playfulness, dullness, strength, wisdom, decline, decrepitude, infirmity, confusion, and finally, the stage of death. (Āyāraṅga Sutta Ṭhāṇa 996)
There are ten types of grass-forest dwellers (taṇavaṇasatikāiya), namely: root, bulb, [and so on] up to flower and fruit, and seed.
All the Vidyādhara ridges are declared to be ten yojanas each in width. All the Ābhiyogika ridges are declared to be ten yojanas each in width.
The Geyika celestial palaces are declared to be one thousand yojanas in height.

In ten situations one may utter speech accompanied by *tejas* (fiery energy), namely: someone might insult a certain ascetic or brahmin; being thus insulted and provoked to anger, he might discharge *tejas* against him; that *tejas* torments him; having tormented him, he utters speech accompanied by that very *tejas*.

Someone might insult such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa; and that [śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa], being thus insulted, might discharge his fiery energy (*tejas*) at the god who is provoked. That [god] would cause him suffering; having caused him suffering, he would utter a cry together with that very fiery energy. Someone might insult such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa; and that [śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa], being thus insulted, is provoked, and the god is also provoked—both of them, acting in opposition, would discharge their fiery energy at him. They would cause him suffering; having caused him suffering, they would both utter a cry together with that very fiery energy.

If someone should insult such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa, and being thus insulted, he becomes enraged and hurls his fiery energy (*tejas*) at him, then boils arise there; those boils burst, and once the boils have burst, they emit a sound along with that very fiery energy.

If someone should insult such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa, and that [śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa], being thus insulted, becomes enraged as a deity and emits his fiery energy (*tejas*), then pustules arise there; those pustules burst, and once they have burst, they produce a sound together with that very fiery energy.

If someone should provoke such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa, and being thus provoked, he becomes enraged—just as a god might become enraged—the two who have made the challenge against him may discharge their fiery energy (*tejas*) at him. There, boils (*phoḍā*) arise; those boils burst; when those boils have burst, they would emit a sound along with that very fiery energy.

If someone should insult such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa, and being thus insulted, he becomes enraged and emits his *tejas* (fiery energy) against him, there *phoḍas* (boils or eruptions) arise; the rest is exactly as before, up until [the point where] one should speak.

If someone should insult such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa, and being thus insulted, the deity becomes enraged and hurls his fiery energy (tejas) at him; there, pustules arise, those pustules burst, and from them, boils arise; those boils burst, and once the boils have burst, they would emit a sound along with that very fiery energy. These three sections are to be recited.

Suppose someone, while harassing such a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa, were to discharge fiery energy (*teja*). That [energy] would not proceed there, nor would it advance; it would turn back again and again. Having turned back, it would perform a circumambulation from left to right (*āyāhiṇapayāhiṇa*); having performed the circumambulation, it would fly upward into the air. Having flown upward, it would then be repelled and return; having returned, burning that very body over and over again, it would produce a sound together with the fiery energy—just as was the case with the fiery energy of Gosāla Maṅkhaliputta. Ten types of non-decaying [powers] are taught (as follows): [list follows].
The assault, the removal from the womb, the woman as a ford, the unrefined assembly, Kṛṣṇa’s Avarakaṅkā, the crossing [of the ocean] by the moon and sun;
the origin of the Harivaṃśa lineage, the rising of Camara, and the eightfold perfection. (Ṭhāṇa 1002)
In infinite time, there have been ten types of honors for those who have attained self-restraint.

(Thāṇa 1003) In this Jewel-Luminous Earth (*Ratnaprabhā*), the layer of jewels (*ratna-kaṇḍa*) is declared to be ten hundred *yojanas* in thickness. In this Jewel-Luminous Earth, the layer of diamond (*vajra-kaṇḍa*) is declared to be ten hundred *yojanas* in thickness. In the same way, the layers of beryl (*vairulika*), ruby (*lohitākṣa*), emerald (*masāragalla*), swan-egg stone (*haṃsagarbha*), coral (*pulaka*), saugandhika, fire-light stone (*jyotirasa*), collyrium (*añjana*), collyrium-coral (*añjanapulaka*), ruby (*ratna*), gold (*jātarūpa*), aṅka, crystal (*sphaṭika*), and emerald (*riṣṭha*)—just as with the layer of jewels, these sixteen kinds are to be described.
All the islands and oceans are declared to be ten hundred yojanas in depth.
All the great lakes are declared to be ten yojanas in depth.
All the water-pools are declared to be ten yojanas in depth.
The two great rivers, the Sītā and the Sītōyā, are ten yojanas each in width at their mouths.
Under the constellation Kṛttikā, the moon moves in its course in the tenth lunar mansion from the outermost circle.
Under the constellation Anurādhā, the moon moves in its course in the tenth lunar mansion from the innermost circle.
Ten lunar mansions are declared to be conducive to the increase of knowledge (namely):
Mṛgaśīrṣa, Ārdrā, Puṣya, the three Pūrvas, Mūla, Śeṣā (Śravaṇā), Hasta, and Citrā; these ten are conducive to the increase of knowledge. (Ṭhāṇaṅga 1008)

Ten million hundred-thousand species of birth-origins for four-footed terrestrial five-sensed animals are taught; ten million hundred-thousand species of birth-origins for belly-crawling terrestrial five-sensed animals are taught.

Living beings have accumulated, are accumulating, or will accumulate matter that has been transmuted through ten stages into the nature of evil karma (*pāpakarma*). Namely: from matter transmuted at the first moment of the formation of a one-sensed being, up to matter transmuted at the non-first moment of the formation of a five-sensed being. In this same manner apply the categories of accumulation (*ciṇa*), further accumulation (*uvaciṇa*), bondage (*bandha*), activation (*udīra*), experience (*vēya*), and likewise destruction (*nijjarā*).

Infinite aggregates consisting of ten space-points are taught; infinite matter-particles (pudgala) occupying ten space-points are taught; infinite matter-particles with a duration of ten time-units (samaya) are taught; infinite matter-particles with tenfold black color are taught. Likewise, [infinite matter-particles] with [tenfold] colors, smells, tastes, and touches are taught; infinite matter-particles with tenfold roughness are taught.
